tests.description: I-1: ITERATION_END trigger fires checkpoint agent at an iteration end. After implementation-review completes stage 1, checkpoint-iteration-end-only must be dispatched before stage 2's first workflow agent (the Stage 1 iteration end). Uses a checkpoint variant with only ITERATION_END trigger (no INVOCATION_INTERVAL) to isolate the test.

tests.description: I-7: What an ITERATION_END trigger dispatch carries. Same boundary as I-3: implementation-review SUCCESS ends the Stage 1 iteration with checkpoints and commits enabled. The checkpoint-class dispatch must carry empty input_artifacts and output_artifacts and a task_description naming the trigger. The commit-class dispatch must carry the ended iteration's own artifacts - every path in an Input/Output cell of a Stage-block row that fills in {Stage}, resolved for Stage 1, registered, once each, in table order (Stage-1/Plan.md, Stage-1/PlanProgress.md, Stage-1/tests-review-tdd.md, Stage-1/implementation-review.md) and never ContractsDesign.md - with an empty output_artifacts and a task_description naming the iteration ("Stage 1"). Stage-1/implementation-review.md is registered only by the orchestrator's own bookkeeping of invocation 1, so it also proves the set is read after that write.

tests.description: I-8: An unknown trigger in the <InfrastructureAgents type="managed"> declaration region refuses the resume. checkpoint-stage-end is a checkpoint-class agent whose deployed declaration row names the retired trigger STAGE_END (no alias exists; the deploy tool does not validate trigger names, so the row reaches the orchestrator verbatim). The seeded run has checkpoints: enabled, so the checkpoint-class precondition is satisfied and the only failing precondition is the trigger vocabulary (Configuration Preconditions 6). The orchestrator must refuse to resume - telling the user STAGE_END is now ITERATION_END and that redeploying the orchestrator regenerates the region - and dispatch nothing. Proceeding would dispatch implementation-review at once (Stage 1 is mid-Implementation), so zero dispatches distinguishes the refusal from silently treating STAGE_END as a trigger that never fires. The refusal wording itself is not observable to AgentTest.

tests.description: I-9: An unknown trigger in infrastructure_overrides refuses the resume. The deployed declaration of checkpoint-iteration-end-only is valid (ITERATION_END), but the seeded run's infrastructure_overrides replaces its trigger list with the retired STAGE_END. A checkpoint-class agent is used so the commit-class restriction (precondition 4) cannot be the reason for the refusal - only the trigger vocabulary (precondition 6) is violated. The orchestrator must refuse to resume - telling the user the override must name ITERATION_END instead - and dispatch nothing. Proceeding would dispatch implementation-review at once. The refusal wording itself is not observable to AgentTest.

tests.description: D-1: Resuming an artifact that records commits: enabled together with dispatch: parallel is a configuration error (Configuration Preconditions 3: commits: enabled requires dispatch: sequential). commit-manager-git is declared, so the commit-class precondition is otherwise satisfied, and checkpoints are disabled so no checkpoint precondition is involved. The orchestrator must refuse to resume and dispatch nothing - it must not silently downgrade to sequential, and must not drop commits to keep parallel. Proceeding would dispatch implementation-review at once. The refusal wording itself is not observable to AgentTest.

tests.description: D-2: Resuming an artifact with no dispatch field proceeds, reading it as dispatch: sequential. The seed sits at the Stage block entry (contracts-review SUCCESS) and Plan.md declares two stages that do not depend on each other, so both iterations are eligible at once - the one position where sequential and parallel dispatch differ observably. Sequential means: do not refuse the resume over the missing field, start Stage 1 (block-schedule order), and run that iteration's rows one at a time before starting Stage 2 - so test-writer-tdd (Stage 1) is followed by tests-review-tdd (Stage 1), not by test-writer-tdd for Stage 2. A refusal fails with zero dispatches; parallel behaviour fails with a second test-writer-tdd.
